passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: You can see all of your own records. Managers and directors can see the profile and time-off balance of people in their reporting chain, and can run the compliance check on their PTO requests. Your benefits elections and your HR tickets are private to you and HR. Nobody else can see your records. If you ask about someone else's records and you are not in their reporting chain, the answer is that the record can't be shared. Access is based on who you are, not on who you say you are: tools that show HR records check the person signed in. Colleagues on the same team, peers and people in other reporting lines cannot see each other's records, even with good intentions. If a colleague asks you for information from their own record, point them to the HR Portal, where they can see it themselves.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: HR keeps the records needed to employ you: your profile (name, title, department, office, Employment Type, Work Arrangement, manager and hire date), your time-off balances, your benefits elections and any HR tickets you raise. Self-service tools such as the HR Portal show these records. They do not show pay or health details. HR keeps records only as long as they are needed for employment, legal or contractual reasons, and protects them under the Information Security & Acceptable Use policy (RSE-SEC-01). Medical information you share with HR, for example about medical leave or an accommodation, is kept separately from your general HR record and is never shown to your manager.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: You can ask for a copy of the personal data HR holds about you, or ask for a correction, through the HR Service Desk. Most of your information can be checked and updated yourself in the HR Portal, such as your contact details and emergency contacts. For anything you can't change yourself, HR will respond to your request as soon as it can and tell you if any information has to be withheld to protect someone else's privacy.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Ridgeline keeps one policy per topic, and each document owns its own rules. The current set of policies is: RSE-HB-01 Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct; RSE-PTO-01 Paid Time Off Policy; RSE-HOL-01 Holiday Calendar & Observance; RSE-LV-01 Leave of Absence Policy; RSE-RW-01 Remote & Hybrid Work Policy; RSE-LOC-01 Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines; RSE-SEC-01 Information Security & Acceptable Use; RSE-EXP-01 Travel & Expense Reimbursement; RSE-BEN-01 Benefits Summary & Eligibility; RSE-EQ-01 Equipment & Home-Office Stipend; RSE-ONB-01 Onboarding Procedures; and RSE-APR-01 Approval Matrix. Where two documents touch the same subject, one states the rule and the other points to it. For example, the number of PTO days you earn is stated only in the Paid Time Off Policy; the Onboarding Procedures mention PTO but point back to it. The approvers for every kind of request are stated only in the Approval Matrix; other policies name the approver for convenience and point to the matrix as the reference. If you ever find two documents that seem to disagree, tell the HR Service Desk so the wording can be corrected, and follow the document that owns the topic until it is.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: If you have a concern about harassment, discrimination, retaliation, safety or any other breach of this handbook, you can raise it in whichever way you are most comfortable with. You can talk to your manager. You can contact the HR Service Desk at hr@ridgeline.example or through HR Portal > Ask HR. For sensitive matters, contact HR Confidential at hr-confidential@ridgeline.example, which only a small HR team can read. You can also call the ethics line on +1 555 0100, available 24/7, with an anonymous option. You never have to raise a concern with the person it is about. When you raise a concern, say what happened, when and where, who was involved and whether anyone else saw it. You don't need proof, and you don't need to be certain that a rule was broken; it is enough that you have a genuine concern. If you prefer, HR can open an HR ticket for you in the HR Confidential queue, with only a minimal summary recorded, and contact you to discuss the details privately.
